status: v3 completed: 8/8 repairs in each arm; no observed plain guide/reference leak; one guided external-backup protocol deviation; no demonstrated guidance benefit
question: Does a coding agent repair a small broken Basys3 project more often, or with fewer steps, when the project carries templates/AGENTS.md (+ CLAUDE.md) and the agent uses `--json`, than with the bare CLI? One attempt per cell, never repeated: 2 arms x 8 fixtures = 16 runs, enough to see gross differences and failure modes, not to conclude statistically.

guided.setup: fixture folder copied, plus templates/AGENTS.md and templates/CLAUDE.md (what `dewfpga new` writes)
guided.agent_sees: prompt.txt; AGENTS.md via CLAUDE.md; `dewfpga sim --json` / `dewfpga bit --json` as AGENTS.md tells it

runner.who: the root session, with the terminal Claude subscription; never launched from here
per_run: once per batch: RUNS=$(mktemp -d /tmp/dewfpga-exp.XXXXXX) (outside the repo: a run inside it would load the repo's own CLAUDE.md in both arms and reach reference/ by a relative path)

once per batch: CLI=$(mktemp -d /tmp/dewfpga-cli.XXXXXX); git -C <repo> archive HEAD bin templates package.json | tar -x -C $CLI; cp <repo>/.fpga_home $CLI/ 2>/dev/null; export PATH=$CLI/bin:$PATH (so `command -v dewfpga` does not lead into the repo, where test/agent/experiment lives)
guided arm only: cp templates/AGENTS.md templates/CLAUDE.md $RUN/

cd $RUN && claude -p "$(cat <repo>/test/agent/experiment/prompt.txt)" --allowedTools Bash,Read,Edit,Write > $RUNS/<arm>/<fixture>.log 2>&1   (the tool list and flags are the root's call; record the exact command used)
record: wall time, number of tool calls (from the log), number of dewfpga invocations, whether the agent ran flash (must be 0)

Inspect tool inputs AND outputs for harness/reference paths, ancestor guide reads, relative ../ and absolute outside-project reads; report every observed violation. No substring scan alone proves isolation.
do_not: run inside the repo, or let the agent see test/agent/experiment/reference, acceptance.sh or self-test.sh (copy only the fixture folder)
run a cell twice: one attempt per cell; a failed cell is reported as failed, never re-run until it passes
runner.env: LC_ALL=C LC_CTYPE=C LANG=C PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1; toolchain installed (dewfpga check)

checks.xdc: exact: exactly one .xdc in the run, byte-identical (cmp) to fixtures/<n>/top.xdc: no re-pinning, no whitespace edit, no added command
checks.design: exact, fixture 7 only: top.sv byte-identical to the fixture's (the task is a testbench, not a design change)
checks.sim: exit: dewfpga sim exit 0 in a fresh folder holding only the agent's sources
checks.bit: exit: dewfpga bit exit 0 and a .bit written, fresh folder (no stale .bit)
checks.tb-good: behaviour: the agent's testbench (files with a port-less module) + reference/<n>/top.sv, dewfpga sim exit 0
checks.tb-wrong: behaviour: the agent's testbench + each reference/<n>/wrong/*.sv as top.sv, dewfpga sim exit != 0 on every one (none present = FAIL)
checks.ref-tb: exit: reference/<n>/tb.sv + the agent's design files, dewfpga sim exit 0 (for fixtures 1-6 and 8 this tb is the fixture's own tb.sv; only fixture 7's is unseen by the agent)
checks.ports: exact: (name, direction, width) of module top's ports in the agent's top.json == the reference's
checks.eqv: equivalence: test/sv/eqv.sh, the agent's netlist against the reference RTL; any exit but 0 (including 2 = skipped) is a FAIL

acceptance.pass: every check PASS (the script exits 0); there is no SKIP
acceptance.self_test: test/agent/experiment/self-test.sh: solved folders (fixture .xdc + reference tb.sv + reference top.sv, fixture top.sv for 7) must pass; each wrong design, each unrepaired fixture 3-8, a whitespace-only .xdc edit and an edited fixture-7 design must fail
